overview.oneLineTake: The Nvidia earnings bounce is the first test of whether the AI selloff has run its course, with a 5% 10-year yield and Hormuz tension keeping volatility bid.
themes: AI chip stress: Nvidia fell for several sessions on tighter US chip export rules and Jensen Huang's exit, then rallied after hours on its earnings beat. Dow futures and tech were up.
Broad tech and growth weakness: SPY closed at 732.44 (-1.01%) and QQQ at 656.95 (-0.73%) on Nov 17. Salesforce fell 9% and Nike 6.3%. Money is rotating into defensive stocks.
Rates remain a headwind: the 10-year yield was 5.12% on Nov 16, and St. Louis Fed's Musalem said four more hikes may be needed. Yields eased after retail sales.
Anthropic's IPO is expected to price above the $70 to $78 range, a test of AI risk appetite.
risks: Nvidia's after-hours bounce may not hold given the China chip policy and governance overhang.
Middle East: a third US carrier has arrived, a tanker was struck in Hormuz, and crude is near $85.
Homebuilder sentiment is at a 14-year low, and the fear gauge is surging again.
Bitcoin slid to $62,000 on a liquidation cascade, a sign of thin liquidity in risk assets.

intelligence.headline: Nvidia's Earnings Come at a Time of Mounting Tech Turmoil
intelligence.summary: Nvidia's earnings arrive after the close today at perhaps the strangest time possible for the world's most important AI chipmaker. Investors already were questioning the durability of the AI boom. Then the Democrats swept to victory in the US midterm elections this month, raising the prospect of tighter regulation for the tech industry. The scandal that led to the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang last week just added to the global upheaval in the stock market's hottest sector. intelligence.headline: On the Move: Intel, Nvidia, Health Insurers, Red Cat
intelligence.summary: Intel falls 3.3% in premarket trading. Nvidia reduced its stake in the chipmaker by roughly 25% last quarter. Nvidia also cut its holding of Nokia, which declines 4.8% in Helsinki. Nvidia is falling 0.2% before its earnings report, in line with Nasdaq 100 futures in premarket trading. Health insurers are among the top premarket decliners, with Humana, CVS and UnitedHealth dropping more than 2% each. Senator Elizabeth Warren called for breaking up "big medicine" in a post on X. US drone maker Red Cat Holdings plunges 28% after the company says it won't meet its revenue target this year.

intelligence.headline: The Petrodollar Is Being Superseded by the Chip-Dollar
intelligence.summary: The dollar's growing link to US equities and the technology sector is becoming more influential than its historic relationship with Treasuries and the oil business, creating the risk that the currency becomes more volatile, Deutsche Bank strategist Mallika Sachdeva says. "The petrodollar is, rather quickly, being superseded by the chip-dollar. A dollar driven by chips, AI and private capital connections should be inherently riskier."

intelligence.headline: Stablecoin Market Value Declines $12 Billion
intelligence.summary: The market value of stablecoins has declined $12 billion over the past 30 days. The dollar-pegged tokens caught on as crypto exchanges adopted them as a substitute for dollars in trading. Now, with crypto gripped in a selloff, holders are converting the tokens back into traditional currencies and cashing out.
